title: Warnings repeated in many ways, so they might wake up.
subtitle: Why the Quran says it more than once

row.title: care
sub: one of them will reach me

then: Ibn Kathir says the Quran came {idea}as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, in clear Arabic{/idea}. The warnings are varied so people will {reward}leave off sins{/reward}, or so it will {reward}produce acts of obedience that bring them closer to Allah{/reward}.
now: Your mother reminds you for the fifth time to call your grandmother. It feels like nagging. Then one day it lands. {idea}Repetition is how love gets through.{/idea} The Quran repeats for the same reason.
old: I have heard this warning before, so I can skip it.
new: Allah repeats it in different ways because one of them might finally reach me.
try: Next time you read a familiar warning verse, ask: what is it saying to me today?

title: Do not rush; say: my Lord, increase me in knowledge.
subtitle: Listening fully, then asking for more
then: Ibn Abbas said the Prophet ﷺ {trap}went through great pains to retain the revelation{/trap}, moving his tongue quickly with Jibril. Allah made it easier: listen quietly, and We will gather it in your chest. Ibn Uyaynah said {reward}the Prophet ﷺ kept increasing in knowledge until Allah took him{/reward}.
now: You start a course, a hifz plan, a new skill, and try to cram it all in one week. Then you burn out. {idea}Listen, take it in, and keep asking for more.{/idea} Knowledge grows over a lifetime.
old: I need to learn everything quickly or I will lose it.
new: I can learn calmly, trust Allah to keep it in me, and keep asking for more.
try: Say "Rabbi zidni ilma" before you study or read anything today.

title: Adam was given a promise, and he forgot.
subtitle: Forgetting is in the human name
then: Ibn Abbas said {idea}man was named Insan because he was given a covenant, but he forgot it{/idea}. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said "forgot" means he abandoned it. Allah found in him {trap}no firm willpower{/trap}. The story of Adam begins with a very human weakness.
now: You set a goal on 1 January and by February it is gone. You promise yourself no more late-night scrolling, and there you are at 1am. {idea}Forgetting is part of being human{/idea}. The point is what you do when you remember.
old: I keep forgetting my promises, so I must be a bad person.
new: Forgetting is human, starting with Adam. Turning back when I remember is what matters.
try: Write down one promise to Allah you forgot, and renew it today with one small step.

title: The angels bowed to Adam, but Iblis refused.
subtitle: Where the enmity began
then: Ibn Kathir says this shows {reward}how Adam was honored{/reward} and favored over much of creation. The angels prostrated as a sign of honor. {trap}Iblis refused and became arrogant{/trap}. From here began his enmity for Adam and his children.
now: A younger colleague gets promoted over you, and something inside refuses to congratulate them. {trap}That refusal to bow to what Allah decided{/trap} is the oldest sin there is. Notice it when it rises.
old: I have good reasons for not accepting someone else's honor.
new: Refusing what Allah gave someone else is the arrogance of Iblis. I can choose to bow.
try: Congratulate one person today on something you secretly envied them for.

title: This is your enemy: do not let him drive you out.
subtitle: A clear warning, given in advance

row.title: Iblis
sub: enemy to you and your wife

then: Allah told Adam: {trap}this is an enemy to you and your wife{/trap}, Hawwa. Ibn Kathir explains: do not be hasty in doing something that gets you expelled, or {trap}you will be tired, uncomfortable and worried, seeking your living{/trap}. In Paradise there was ease.
now: You know the exact trigger: the late night, the certain app, the particular friend. {idea}The enemy has been named for you already.{/idea} Knowing his face is half the protection.
old: Temptation catches me completely by surprise.
new: Allah already named my enemy. I can learn his tricks and stay alert.
try: Write down your top trigger for doing wrong, and one plan to avoid it this week.

title: Here you will never be hungry or unclothed.
subtitle: Inner and outer need, both covered
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah {idea}combined hunger and nakedness{/idea} because hunger is an inner humiliation and nakedness an outer one. Adam was told {reward}both were taken care of{/reward}. He lacked nothing, inside or out.
now: Your fridge has food. Your wardrobe has clothes. Yet you scroll the sales page feeling like something is missing. {idea}Notice what is already covered{/idea}, before the whisper of "more" arrives.
old: I will be content once I get the next thing.
new: Much of what I need is already given. Seeing that makes me harder to trick.
try: Before buying anything non-essential today, name three things you already have.

title: No thirst there, and no burning sun.
subtitle: The other half of the promise
then: Ibn Kathir notes these two are also a pair: {idea}thirst is an inner heat, the sun's heat an outer one{/idea}. With this, every basic need was covered. Adam had {reward}complete ease{/reward}, and only one tree was off limits.
now: Your marriage is good, your job is fine, your health is okay. Then one forbidden thing starts to look like the only thing that matters. {idea}One small limit can feel bigger than all the gifts.{/idea}
old: The one thing I cannot have is the thing I need most.
new: I have so much. One limit is not worth risking all of it.
try: When one forbidden thing pulls at you today, list five gifts you would risk for it.

title: Shall I show you the tree of forever?
subtitle: The whisper always offers something bigger
then: Shaytan whispered to Adam about {trap}the tree of eternity and a kingdom that never decays{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes another verse where he {trap}swore he was a sincere well-wisher{/trap}. He kept prodding until they ate from it.
now: "This deal will set you up for life." "Just this once, it will make you happy forever." "I am only saying this because I care about you." {idea}Temptation rarely sounds like an enemy.{/idea} It sounds like a friend promising forever.
old: I would recognise a temptation easily if it came.
new: The whisper dresses up as advice and promises what it cannot give.
try: When something promises you "forever" or "everything" today, slow down and question it.

title: They ate, felt exposed, and reached for leaves.
subtitle: The first shame after the first slip
then: Adam and his wife ate, and {trap}what had been covered became exposed{/trap}. Mujahid said they {idea}patched the leaves on themselves like a garment{/idea}. Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred. The promised kingdom turned out to be shame.
now: The moment after: closing the tab, deleting the message, feeling hot in the face. {trap}The promise was pleasure; the result is wanting to hide.{/trap} That feeling is not the end. Look at the next verse.
old: After I slip, all I can do is hide and cover it up.
new: Shame after a slip is real. Adam's story shows it is not the last chapter.
try: After your next slip, do not hide it from Allah. Tell Him what you did in plain words.

title: Then his Lord chose him, forgave him, and guided him.
subtitle: The slip was not the end of Adam
then: Right after "Adam disobeyed" comes {reward}then his Lord chose him, turned to him with forgiveness, and guided him{/reward}. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith where Musa blamed Adam, and Adam answered that {idea}it had been written for him before he was created{/idea}.
now: You made a mistake that everyone in your family still brings up. You feel defined by it. {reward}Allah's last word on Adam was not the tree.{/reward} It was chosen, forgiven, guided.
old: My worst mistake is who I am.
new: Allah can choose me, forgive me and guide me after my worst slip.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one mistake you feel defined by, and then let it rest.

title: Follow My guidance: no going astray, no misery.
subtitle: The promise given at the descent
then: Allah sent Adam, Hawwa and Iblis down, {trap}some of you enemies to others{/trap}. Then the promise: guidance will come. Abu Al-Aliyah said that means {idea}the Prophets, the Messengers and the evidence{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said the follower {reward}will not be misguided here or distressed in the Hereafter{/reward}.
now: Life on earth is the office politics, the traffic, the family fights. It is not Paradise. But {idea}guidance was promised for exactly this place{/idea}, and you are holding it in your hand right now.
old: Life here is just hard and I am on my own.
new: Allah sent guidance for this hard place. Following it keeps me from getting lost.
try: Pick one verse from this surah and live by it for the rest of the day.

title: Turn from My remembrance, and life gets tight.
subtitle: Comfort outside, tightness inside

row.title: outside
sub: eats, wears, lives as he likes

then: Ibn Kathir explains a life of hardship means {trap}no tranquillity and no ease in the chest{/trap}. Even if he looks comfortable, eating and wearing what he likes, {trap}his heart is in agitation and doubt{/trap}. Mujahid said being raised blind means having no proof.
now: Nice flat, good salary, holidays twice a year, and still that heavy feeling on Sunday nights. {idea}Tightness of chest is not fixed by more stuff.{/idea} Remembering Allah is what widens it.
old: If I had more money and comfort, I would feel at peace.
new: Peace lives in the chest, and it comes from remembering Allah.
try: When you feel that tightness today, stop and do two minutes of dhikr.
